title: Proteus: a closed-loop network defense driven by a simulated C. elegans connectome
description: A deterministic C99 simulator of a 279-neuron C. elegans connectome (graded potentials, short-term synaptic plasticity, neuromodulators, body physics) runs inside a network daemon. Port moves and firewall bans are a readout of that nervous system's state rather than a seeded PRNG. The release includes the vendored biophysical engine, the detection/reflex layer, journals with bitwise replay, preregistered hypotheses with falsification criteria, and the negative results: biology is not more random than a PRNG at a 64-symbol alphabet, the PRNG arm's seed is recoverable from three observations, and the current connectome readout is rank one.
